title: How we are supercharging Test, Learn and Grow through movement building
authors: Steff Riches - Network and Engagement Lead for Test, Learn and Grow, Cabinet Office

content.text: When we launched Test, Learn and Grow, our goal was simple: prove that testing small, learning rapidly, and adapting as you go is a credible, effective approach to public service reform.

Through our multidisciplinary accelerator teams working side-by-side with places, we’ve seen what happens when you give frontline staff and communities the space to have their voices heard and the freedom to innovate.

We also know how valuable it is when different skills and capabilities are recognised and valued, but that there are foundational conditions of the system which sometimes mean this work can be difficult and we need collaboration between many people to make a difference.

True system change doesn't rely on a single central team or a fixed project timeline. It happens when you supercharge a national movement of champions, practitioners, and supporters across the whole system who adopt agile and innovative ways of working as second nature.

We are planting many of the seeds of our movement in fertile ground that has been prepared by lots of people who have been working on this, and creating change long before the programme and movement existed and we continue to look to them for inspiration.

The TLG Conveners are Catherine Howe (Chief Executive, Dorset Council), Beth Russell (Second Permanent Secretary, HM Treasury), Paul Morrison (Director General, Home Office), and Emma De Closset (Chief Executive, UK Community Foundations). If you are connected to our movement you will get opportunities to hear from them directly through our events and convening work.
The movement is open to anyone who is curious about learning together, in any place, sector or seniority. The diversity of our collective insight is what builds strength, confidence and evidence.
